newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says tax event organisers at venue.
newsitem.headline: Court says tax event organisers at venue.

text.p: The European Court of Justice has ruled that entertainment organisers should be taxed in the country where they stage their event rather than where their business is established.
A German sound engineer who organises performances challenged Bonn tax authorities who wanted to consider his income regardless of where it was earned.

The Sixth VAT directive article 9(2)(c) clearly states that services relating to entertainment are supplied where they are physically carried out. These services include the activities of organisers as well as those providing ancillary services.
But the German tax authorities argued that sound and light engineers fell outside the scope of services ancillary to the entertainment provided.
The court said the level of artistic talent is not at issue, and all services relating to merely similar activities fall within the scope of the exception in article 9(2)(c).
The court reasoned the purpose of taxing certain services in the place they are carried out is to establish a special system of services.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Sixth VAT directive - Interpretation of article 9(2)(c) - Sound-engineering for artistic or entertainment events - Place where the services are supplied"
Reference from the Finanzgericht, Cologne (Germany) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between

on the interpretation of article 9(2) of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnvoer taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1)

1. The first indent of article 9(2) of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnvoer taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment must be interpreted as covering the activity of a person who provides sound-engineering for artistic or entertainment events by choosing and operating the equipment used, adjusting it to the particualr acoustic conditions and the desired sound effects, and who supplies the requisite equipment and operating staff, where the service which he provides constitutes a prerequisite for the perfomance of the principal artistic or entertaiment service supplied.

2. The fact that the person concerned has undertaken in addition to coordinate the sound effects to be produced with his assistance with certain visual effects produced by other persons cannot affect the answer given to the first question.
